graft.title: Capability vocabulary: kvm (and arch:/os: if they're meant to be used)
graft.need: estate/capabilities.toml has no `kvm` (nor `nixos-test`, `arch:x86_64`, `arch:aarch64`, `os:linux`, `os:darwin`), so vg-dotfiles can't state it in its `nix#estate` capabilities, and the file says an id is added before it's used. Needed: `kvm` (a Linux machine with /dev/kvm usable for NixOS VM tests), and arch:/os: ids if the vocabulary is meant to carry them (thalam's graft to vg-dotfiles names them as examples). Once they exist, vg-dotfiles sets them where its modules turn them on.
graft.use_case: thalam (graft 01a19b0c to vg-dotfiles) reads each machine's capabilities only from vg-dotfiles' `estate` export, and tend places a project's checks by `needs = ["kvm"]` (NixOS VM tests, Jacquard's flake check). vg-dotfiles now exports `capabilities` per host with the ids the vocabulary has (nix, vulkan, opencl, tenstorrent); without `kvm` no machine can be matched for a VM test.

answer.text: Planned: kvm (a Linux machine with /dev/kvm usable for NixOS VM tests) is added to estate/capabilities.toml, where the needs vocabulary lives until the estate moves to thalam. Whether arch:/os: ids belong in the vocabulary is left to the user; the todo says so.
